# Manim Video

Curated by Skill Harbor: a Manim video skill for turning technical concepts into clean animated explainers instead of generic talking-head scripts. The workflow starts where good video starts: define the core visual thesis in one sentence, break the concept into 3 to 6 scenes, decide what each scene proves, and write the scene outline before writing any Manim code. Scene planning rules keep things tight: each scene proves one thing, avoid overstuffed diagrams, prefer progressive reveal over full-screen clutter, use motion to explain state change rather than to keep the screen busy, and keep title cards short and loaded with meaning. Render conventions cover the practical side (render the smallest working version first, then tighten typography, spacing, color, and pacing), with a default output of a short 16:9 MP4 plus a thumbnail frame, and handoff guidance to the wider video stack (video-editing, remotion-video-creation) only when it adds value. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: requires the manim CLI and ffmpeg installed locally; rendering takes real time, especially at high quality; best for precise technical visuals, not cinematic footage. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
